title: Solid, Liquid or Gas?
summary: Three states of matter, and how heating and cooling change one into another.

steps.title: Three states
sentences: Everything around us is made of matter, and matter comes in three common states.
A solid keeps its shape, like a stone.
A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container, like water, and a gas spreads out to fill all the space, like air.

steps.title: Tiny particles
sentences: All matter is made of tiny particles.
In a solid they are packed close and only wiggle in place.
In a liquid they slide past each other, and in a gas they zoom around far apart.

steps.title: Change by heating
sentences: When you heat ice, it melts into water.
When you heat water, it boils and becomes steam.
When you cool steam it condenses to water, and when you cool water enough it freezes to ice.

steps.title: Try it at home
sentences: Put an ice cube in a bowl and watch it melt.
Notice the puddle of water it makes.
With an adult's help, watch a covered pot of hot water make drops on the lid, that is condensation.
points: Always have an adult near heat

facts: Water is unusual because ice floats on water.
Steam itself is invisible: the white cloud you see above a kettle is tiny drops of water.
Most of the visible universe, like the Sun, is made of a fourth state called plasma.

quiz.q: Which state of matter keeps its own shape?
What is it called when water turns to ice?
In which state are the particles farthest apart?
quiz.why: In a gas the particles are far apart and move freely.
